newsitem.title: USA: Michigan cites Home Depot for mispricing.
newsitem.headline: Michigan cites Home Depot for mispricing.

text.p: Home Depot Inc. Monday was cited by Michigan Attorney General Frank Kelley for failing to price its merchandise properly or correctly.
Failure to comply could lead to a lawsuit, with a maximum penalty of $25,000 for knowing and persistent violations, Kelley said.
The giant do-it-yourself chain, which has 10 days to respond to the notice, said it was working to comply with the state's item pricing requirements.
Michigan state authorities in 1995 found that Home Depot stores in Canton Township, Northville, Pontiac and Utica, Mich., failed to item price almost all consumer goods as required under state law.

The stores failed to comply with the law by October and November 1996, despite verbal assurances that they would do so. In addition, investigators found that items that were priced properly did not reflect the correct price when scanned at the cash register.

"The company noted Massachusetts and Michigan are the only states where Home Depot does business using unit pricing, and further notes that all of its stores have merchandise clearly and conspicuously marked by shelving pricing and UPC (Universal Pricing Code) bar codes," Home Depot said.

"The Home Depot abides by the Michigan law and will quickly put in place the additional pricing information. The company is meeting with the attorney general's office to assure continuing compliance."
